Today’s release of macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 includes a brand new dynamic wallpaper of the Golden Gate Bridge, bringing the total number of dynamic wallpapers to five. Download links for all are provided below.

The macOS 27 Golden Gate desktop wallpaper library continues to grow

When Apple announced macOS 27 Golden Gate at WWDC26, it showed the same system wallpaper on all operating systems, featuring a stylized 27.

However, after several developer betas, Apple began adding a dynamic screensaver, which can also be used as a desktop wallpaper, featuring a beautiful slow-motion video looking down on San Francisco’s famous Golden Gate Bridge.

After your Mac is unlocked, the screensaver will slowly come to a stop, each time leaving behind a brand new but slightly different desktop wallpaper.

Although the dynamic effects are handled by macOS, below you will see a static frame from each of the four videos, along with the light and dark versions of the stylized 27 desktop wallpaper.

Be sure to click the images to save the highest-resolution version. To set it as your background, you can go to System Settings > Wallpaper, scroll down to “Your Photos,” click the “Add Photo” button, and then do any of the following:

Add a photo from your Photos library: Click “Choose from Photos,” then select a photo. Add an image file: Click “Choose File,” select a file, then click “Open”. You can also drag an image from your desktop or a folder directly onto the thumbnail at the top of the Wallpaper settings. Add a folder from Finder: Click “Choose Folder,” select a folder, then click “Open”. Add an album or folder from the Photos app: Pick an album or folder under “Photo Collections.”

According to Apple, “You can also use a custom wallpaper without opening the Wallpaper settings”:

Use a photo from your Photos library: Open the Photos app, select a photo, click the share button in the Photos toolbar, then click “Set as Wallpaper.” Use an image found online: In a Safari window, Control-click the image and select “Use Image as Desktop Picture.” Use an image saved on your Mac: Click the Finder icon in the Dock to open a Finder window. Control-click the image file, then click “Set as Desktop Picture.”

To learn more about how to set custom wallpapers in macOS, please click this link.
